brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer at a corner of cell 0,0,0
requirements.evidence: drawer:0#0,0#cut on piece:0,0,0;half-n (south cut) — half base provides cut face for drawer

requirements.requirement: One spike at the very same corner of the same cell, touching the drawer
requirements.evidence: Config refused spike at junction [(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)] level 0 with SPIKE_CLASH: 'a drawer (south half) fills this corner of the junction, where the spike would stand.' Reverse order also fails — spike and drawer are mutually exclusive at same junction by configurator rule. Spike socket s49 exists but cannot be placed together with drawer.

finish.summary: Built 3-cell L with half-n at 0,0 to host drawer at its south cut (corner shared by 0,0 / 0,1 / 1,0). Placing drawer succeeded; adding spike at identical junction was refused with SPIKE_CLASH. Rule prevents both occupying same corner simultaneously. Left drawer installed to demonstrate location; spike cannot be added without removing drawer.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
